abstract: This ASTP Health IT Data Brief examines trends in hospital adoption and use of predictive AI from 2023 to 2024 using American Hospital Association survey data. The analysis reveals that predictive AI adoption in U.S. non-federal acute care hospitals increased from 66% to 71% between 2023 and 2024, with the fastest growth in administrative applications including billing automation (36% to 61%) and scheduling facilitation (51% to 67%). Despite overall increases, significant disparities persist across hospital types, with small, rural, independent, and critical access hospitals lagging in adoption, and most hospitals conducting evaluation for accuracy and bias while reporting multiple entities accountable for AI governance.
keyFindings: Hospital adoption of predictive AI increased from 66% in 2023 to 71% in 2024, with 82% of hospitals in 2024 evaluating models for accuracy and 74% for bias.

Billing automation use surged 25 percentage points (36% to 61%) and scheduling automation grew 16 percentage points (51% to 67%) between 2023 and 2024, representing the fastest-growing predictive AI use cases.

System-affiliated hospitals used predictive AI at significantly higher rates (86% in 2024) compared to independent hospitals (37%), and hospitals using the market-leading EHR vendor (90%) greatly outpaced other vendors (50%).
Hospitals used EHR-developed AI most frequently (80% in 2024), followed by third-party AI (52%) and self-developed AI (50%), with variation in use cases depending on source.

74% of hospitals reported multiple entities were accountable for evaluating predictive AI, with specialized committees or task forces (66%) and division/department leaders (60%) being most commonly responsible.
methodology: Data from the American Hospital Association (AHA) Information Technology Supplement surveys conducted in 2023 and 2024. The 2024 survey (fielded April-September 2024) included 2,080 non-federal acute care hospitals with a 51% response rate (N=2,253 respondents). The 2023 survey (fielded March-August 2023) had 2,425 respondents with a 58% response rate. Hospital-level weights were derived using inverse propensity scoring based on hospital characteristics including size, ownership, teaching status, system membership, urban status, and region. Analysis includes descriptive statistics, comparisons across hospital characteristics, and assessment of evaluation practices and governance structures.
qualifiers: Response rates of 51% (2024) and 58% (2023) may introduce bias. Survey limited to non-federal acute care hospitals in the 50 states and District of Columbia. Missing and 'don't know' responses (up to 21% for bias evaluation questions in 2024) were excluded from denominators. Post-implementation evaluation or monitoring was not included in the 2023 survey instrument. Authors note findings represent 'early evidence' and that 'ongoing challenges persist with AI implementation' including demonstrating real-world performance and engaging clinical workforce. Small hospitals, rural hospitals, and those not using market-leading EHR vendors are underrepresented in high-adoption groups.
